summary: Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a Buddhist Studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Isebaert is a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Albert Joris van Windekens from circa 1975 to 1981 and became a professor at Université catholique de Louvain around 1983.

Lambert Schmithausen is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1957–1963) and Paul Hacker (~1963–1966). He was associate professor of Indology at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and served on the Advisory Board at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lan Wu works in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University (2008–2016) and held posts at the University of New Mexico (Assistant Professor, 2015–2016) and Mount Holyoke College (Associate Professor, 2023).

Lance E. Nelson is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986. He served as professor (attested 1994–2012) and Professor Emeritus (2021) at the University of San Diego.

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–2000) and Oxford (~2000–2015), and served as president of the UKABS and Pali Text Society.
Lancelot Wilkinson was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College (~1821–1823) and joined the Bombay Civil Service in 1822.
Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned a PhD from Yale University, where she studied under Janet Gyatso, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Lang Eun Ra specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. As a doctoral student at Temple University, she studied under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Langdon Warner was an art historian and archaeologist specializing in Sinology and Japanology. Educated at Harvard (A.B. ~1899–1903), he directed the American School of Archaeology in China (1913–1914) and Philadelphia Museum of Art (1917–1923), and lectured at Harvard (~1923–1950).

Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and later became Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism there (attested 2026).

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities. He held teaching posts there, at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the University of Washington, and was affiliated with Langara College (attested 2005).

Lars Edman was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Uppsala University (1847–1857), where he became docent in Oriental languages in 1857 and served as associate professor of German and English languages from 1863 to 1892.

Lars Fogelin works in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (~1971–1984), Heidelberg, and Bonn. He held positions at the University of Oslo (~1990–1997, attested 2002–2008) and Middle East Technical University (attested 2000).

Lars Nannestad Boisen was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (1819–1827), Halle, and Bonn, learning under Georg Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, Christian Lassen, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

Lata Chhatre is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She served at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and as Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lata Deokar works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her MA (1992–1995) and PhD (2001–2014) at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, worked at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2000–2012), and is Visiting Faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).
